text:
alyssa: heads up — canary for the Dedicated rollout spiked p95 starting ~08:15 UTC after yesterday's runtime merge (PR #8543). SLA risk, customers might see timeouts. :exclamation:

kevin: any idea which part? kernel selection, batching, or cache?

alyssa: perf-bot flagged a CI perf regression on the dedicated-end2end-perf job: p95 +14% and cpu time +22%. It's correlated with the merge that changed the batching heuristic default and added the new kernel selector heuristic.

perf-bot: [automated] dedicated-end2end-perf/ci failed: p95 latency increase = +14.3% (baseline 170ms -> 194ms). Regression likely between commits c3f7..f1a2.

mina: re: kernel selector — the new heuristic prefers tiled-matmul for sequence lengths > 32. In canary we're mostly short seqs (<=32) but batch sizes jumped due to continuous batching change. Selector ended up picking tiled kernels for short seqs which are slower.

dave: that explains it. tiled kernels have higher launch overhead for short sequences. If batching packs short requests into larger batches the selector mis-estimates shape distribution.

kevin: can we reproduce locally? share the failing perf CI commit range and the command used.

alyssa: repro script I used:
```bash
git checkout f1a2a3b
make perf-stress TARGET=dedicated-canary SEQ_DIST=short BATCH_SCHEDULE=continuous_heuristic
./perf-run --model gpt-small --iters 500 --measure p95
```
results: baseline commit c3f7: p95=168ms, commit f1a2: p95=195ms.

mina: I ran a quick flamegraph. Kernel-level shows a big jump in time in `matmul_tiled_launch` and `prefetch_kv_shard` during iterative batches. Looks like KV cache gets smaller effective locality because batching interleaves requests — eviction churn increases.

alyssa: attaching short snippets from /tmp/perf.tar.gz (uploaded to #artifacts). Key lines:
```
# flame slice (short requests)
matmul_tiled_launch  42%\nmatmul_nontiled      9%\nkv_cache_evict       18%\nallocator_wait       7%\n```

oncall: this is risky for Dedicated customers — we have an upcoming rollout window in 3 hours. Recommend hold until a mitigation or revert.

kevin: propose two short-term options:
1) revert PR #8543 (last resort)
2) patch selector to prefer non-tiled for seq <=32 or when measured batch shape variance > threshold
3) disable continuous batching temporarily for Dedicated canary only (config flag)

mina: I can put together a patch for option 2. Quick heuristic: if batch_histogram.short_frac > 0.6 then force kernel=matmul_nontiled. Patch diff (sketch):
```diff
@@ -runtime/kernel_selector.py +runtime/kernel_selector.py
-    if score_tiled > score_nontiled: select = 'tiled'
+    # avoid tiled for short-dominant batches (reverts perf regression)
+    if batch_stats.short_frac > 0.6:
+        select = 'nontiled'
+    elif score_tiled > score_nontiled:
+        select = 'tiled'
```

alyssa: can you also add a metric gate so perfbot refuses a rollout if p95 delta > 8%?

mina: adding gate to rollout service now. PR incoming.

perf-bot: perf-check: running historical diff for c3f7..f1a2 — p95 delta +14.3% (CI). Blocking rollout per perf gate (threshold 10%).

kevin: short-term I want to flip Dedicated config to disable continuous batching on canary only. That should reduce shape variance and avoid selector flip. I'll push config change and patch kernel selector as follow-up.

dave: also add KV cache diagnostic counters to the canary (evict_rate, hit_locality) — we need better telemetry next time.

alyssa: agreed. I'll open a customer comms note and tag support. For now: hold rollout, revert disabled = false.

oncall: updated the Dedicated canary to continuous_batching=false (canary-config-2026-03-18). Monitoring.

mina: PR 8621 created with the kernel selector guard + perf test. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8621

kevin: thanks. Once PR is green and perf checks back within threshold we can unhold. Until then, rollback flagged as option but prefer targeted fix.

alyssa: marking this thread as rollout-blocker. I'll follow up with timeline. :lock:
